title: The Bumpkin — Sc089: top-shot tableau — Nicole, Anais and Darwin flat on the ground (KeyAnim)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Top-shot staging in a KeyAnim file: the camera looks straight down at a grey ground plate (GB222_BUMPKIN_Sc089_LO_BG.jpg) and three characters lie flat in a diagonal row — Nicole centre, Anais lower-left, Darwin right — each on their own scene layer, for 177 frames. The export shows the production split honestly: the heads are finished colour face comps and carry a full dialogue scene (Anais talks through f23-89, Darwin answers f111-155, Nicole's shifting reactions carry f133-177) while every body below the neck is still red rough construction lines in every frame. Three head comps on a held overhead tableau are the whole scene.
notes: No Gumball in this scene: the cast is Nicole, Anais and Darwin only, each on its own scene layer named for its puppet — a Watterson scene built entirely without him.
The bodies never clean up in the export: red rough limbs are visible in every sampled frame — this is the KeyAnim state of the file, recorded as-is.
Almost no staging motion across 177 frames: the tableau is held and only mouths, eyes and slight head tilts change (face comps 3,206 kf vs 868 body kf).
The 63.9 MB FLA is the largest file in the batch, but the bulk is library head/face-comp depth, not scene complexity: only 15 animated symbols.
Render took two FFDec attempts (172/177 cached, then complete).
